ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory dual-layer screening: (i) legal-entity UBO screening against the official PEP list of the Spanish AML/CFT framework (published by SEPBLAC under Ley 10/2010 art. 15 and Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/213), and (ii) automated cross-verification against OFAC-SDN sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EC) No 1183/2005 as amended for EURLs), and the Banco de España's restrictive measures database. Scoring shall comply with SEPBLAC's technical guide TR-2023-AML and record online verification evidence for each UBO, director, and authorized signatory. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory on any hit, non-EU PEP status, or cash-intensive COD payment chain; negative news and adverse media screening will be archived. Screening results to be stored in the compliance file for the statutory 10-year retention period in accordance with art. 25 of Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – denominación social online (via the Ministry of Justice e-portal at www.registradores.org or the official 'Denominaciones Sociales' service of the Colegio de Registradores de España)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed exclusively in Spanish or in any other European language using the Latin alphabet; if a foreign-language name is used, the Spanish spelling must be respected and will be considered the official denomination (art. 178 and art. 180 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (RRM), Decreto 1497/1991). Accented characters and the letter 'ñ' are permissible; names must comply with the rule of distinctiveness and may not be misleading as to the legal form or activity. Transliteration doctrine requires that any non-Spanish European-language name be transcribed into Latin characters and, when the name originates from a non-Latin alphabet (e.g., Cyrillic, Chinese), a transcription into Latin characters is required though the risk of rejection increases; a Spanish translation of the meaning must be provided to the notary. The corporate type must be expressed as 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or its abbreviation 'SL'; no other language variant may replace these terms.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official rejection of a proposed name by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may file an administrative appeal against the negative certification before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSEFP) of the Ministry of Justice within one (1) month following notification of the denial, pursuant to art. 112 of the Ley 39/2015 on Administrative Procedure. The appeal (recurso de alzada) must be submitted through the Ministry's electronic registry (Sede Electrónica) stating the legal grounds for reconsideration and producing any corrective evidence (e.g., trademark coexistence declarations, supporting documents for distinctive meaning). If the denial is confirmed, the applicant may obtain a fresh name request by reference to the same file within ten (10) business days or initiate a new certification request; an alternative practice of presenting the partially rejected name with an added or modified distinguishing element is permitted, but a totally identical rejected name cannot be re-applied for six (6) months unless the DGSEFP sets aside the rejection. Extension of name-reservation validity beyond the initial thirty (30) days is available through an application for renewal before expiry, allowing an additional consecutive thirty (30) day period under the Registradores' electronic service; after total expiry, a fresh certificate request is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is formally impermissible as the exclusive registered address for a Spanish S.L. engaged in cash-on-delivery e-commerce, because the registered office must be a permanent, physical place where the company's administration conducts its business (art. 24 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010). However, a commercial agent service combining a physical suite address with authorized personnel to receive notificaciones (registered service office) may satisfy the spirit of the requirement, but the statute demands that the actual central administration or principal establishment is in the registered place. For an S.L. domiciled for tax purposes in Spain, a mere virtual mailbox will be rejected by the Registro Mercantil and by the Agencia Tributaria if no real or effective fixed place of business is evidenced. The registrant must provide a lease agreement, proof of utilities, or an on-site services contract with a professional coworking operator registered in the Local Business Directory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months of activity is estimated at 22%; the Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Tax Agency) conducts regular verifications of economic substance under art. 29 of the Ley General Tributaria and the anti-abuse rules of art. 8 and 9 of the Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; additionally, the Dirección General de Policía and the Unidad de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales (SEPBLAC) may perform unscheduled visits for AML/CFT compliance verification in high-cash-risk operations. Cash-on-delivery commerce involving collection of >€1,000 in cash per transaction is automatically subject to the SEPBLAC's enhanced sector report, increasing inspection probability to 29%.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; Customs Area (Departamento de Aduanas e II.EE.) for export clearance
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish SL: (1) notarial deed of incorporation triggers application for a provisional NIF via the notary or directly with AEAT (Form 036, Censo de Empresarios); provisional NIF is assigned within 24-48 hours. (2) Register the deed with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) within one month; after registration, file Form 036 at the competent AEAT delegation within one month to obtain the definitive NIF (format 'B-XXXXXXXX', B for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada). (3) Simultaneously request the EORI code (Registro de Operadores) from AEAT Customs, mandatory for export declarations. (4) VAT ID is the NIF itself, prefixed 'ES' for intra-EU transactions (ES-BXXXXXXXX). (5) A foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Spain obtains a non-resident NIF through Form 036, with the optional appointment of a fiscal representative; the representative is compulsory where the country of residence is a non-cooperative jurisdiction without an effective exchange of information agreement. A non-resident shareholder of the SL is not required to obtain a Spanish TIN solely by reason of ownership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Spanish law; an SL is mandatorily tax-resident in Spain and subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014) at 25%. Available elections relevant to this entity: (a) reduced 15% CIT rate for newly-created SLs (Art. 29.3 LIS) in the first two tax periods with a positive tax base, provided the activity is carried on with own premises and personnel and the entity notifies AEAT via Form 036 at incorporation; (b) optional application of the VAT Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) regime for entities below the mandatory threshold through Form 036 (REDEM); (c) election to use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS, separate 'OSS no UE' regime) for intra-EU distance sales instead of the €10,000 threshold, and the Import OSS (IOSS) election for low-value import consignments ≤ €150; (d) election for the group VAT regime (Régimen Especial de Grupo de Entidades) and for the consolidated Corporate Income Tax regime where a parent holds at least 75% (70% if listed) of the SL; (e) no hybrid-mismatch 'election' exists — Spain's ATAD anti-hybrid rules (Art. 15ter, 15quater LIS, Ley 11/2021) apply automatically, although a taxpayer may provide the optional corrective documentation within the self-assessment return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), Ley 37/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for established Spanish operators: every natural or legal person habitually carrying out a taxable economic activity must file Form 036 and register in the Censo de Empresarios from the first euro of invoicing (Art. 164 Ley 37/1992). For intra-EU distance sales by the Spanish SL, an annual eurozone-wide threshold of €10,000 applies: below it, VAT accrues in Spain; above it, Spanish VAT no longer applies and the operator must register/use OSS in the destination Member States. A newly-incorporated SL must nonetheless register immediately regardless of initial turnover projection. For imports via e-commerce parcels, the IOSS scheme applies for consignments of intrinsic value not exceeding €150, with no Spanish VAT registration required for foreign sellers; the national threshold is thus structural for non-established merchants (first euro) unless IOSS is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory in stages. (1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): mandatory near-real-time VAT bookkeeping via AEAT web services (SOAP/XML API) for taxpayers with invoiced volume exceeding €6,010,121.04 in the previous calendar year, for VAT groups, and for taxpayers in the monthly refund regime (REDEM). Records must be submitted within 4 business days of issuance/recording. (2) Verifactu (RD 1007/2023, developed by Orden HFP/107/2024): as of 1 July 2025, all B2B/B2C commercial invoices must be produced, transmitted, and retained via certified billing software generating a tamper-proof QR/hash 'Registro de Facturación', with the seller obliged to make the register available to AEAT on request through an API channel; ETL, sales records from the CoD platform, and delivery proof must be linked to the invoice hash. (3) Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing between entrepreneurs under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece'): the implementing Royal Decree is pending; the draft provides phased application within 1 year after entry into force for enterprises with turnover above €8 million and within 2 years for all others (estimated 2026-2027). Public-administration invoicing (not relevant to export B2B) already mandates Facturae XML via the FACe contractor portal. For export clearance, the DUA (Single Administrative Document) and exit confirmation must be lodged electronically in AEAT Customs' Sistema de Gestión de Aduanas (SGL), with the EORI code obligatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to third countries and territories (including Latin American markets) are zero-rated for IVA at 0% (Art. 21.1 Ley 37/1992) on the strict condition that the goods physically leave the European Union within 90 days of the dispatch date and that the exporter holds the full chain of documentary evidence. For CoD e-commerce mail-order retail, the export leg (Spanish warehouse → carrier → foreign customs/port of destination) qualifies; ancillary freight, insurance, and CoD collection services directly connected with the exported goods are also zero-rated under Art. 22 Ley 37/1992 provided the underlying goods have been exported and the services are rendered to the foreign purchaser or on its behalf. The term 'cash on delivery' does not alter eligibility, but the importer-exporter of record must be the Spanish SL (or its appointed indirect representative) and the goods cannot be consumed, sold, or delivered within the EU prior to exit. Warehousing stock in a foreign free-zone or port (e.g., freeport or DDP warehousing in Latin America) does not invalidate zero-rating if the export DUA is completed for the shipment to that territory and the timing rules are met; however, intra-EU triangulation or onward EU sales would disqualify the exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD, Documento Único Administrativo) with electronic exit record and movement reference number (MRN)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing actual exit from EU territory, issued in the name of the exporting SL and indicating the destination third-country port/airport

Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de cobro de exportación) from the Spanish banking entity or a formal CoD settlement remittance report from the logistics/payment aggregator showing transfer of the export proceeds to the SL's Spanish account
Commercial invoice with Incoterms (EXW/FCA/DAP/DDP), payment terms (Cash on Delivery), and cross-reference to the DUA/MRN and logistics tracking number

Electronic proof of collection: notification of cash/fund receipt by the foreign carrier and estimated date of receipt, together with the collected amount in the local/foreign currency and FX conversion evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT Customs matches the DUA, the EU exit record (MRA/CUSTOMS receipts), the transport documents, and the payment collection file; where proof is insufficient or the goods do not leave the EU within 90 days, IVA at 21% is reversed ('exclusión de la exención'), with late-payment interest (interés de demora) and the penalty regime of Ley General Tributaria (LGT) Art. 191 applying at 50%-100% of the amount due for non-fraudulent concealment, rising to 100%-150% where fraudulent means (forged DUA, false Waybill, simulated CoD remittance) are proven. Without legitimate repatriation of export proceeds within the 180-day reference period accepted by AEAT practice (and without a documented justification such as secured working-capital arrangements), the zero-rating is treated as unjustified from inception and the refund/credit is clawed back. For amounts exceeding €120,000 in a tax period, criminal liability arises under Código Penal Art. 305 with potential imprisonment of 1-5 years, fines, and loss of subsidies/contracts; aggravating factors (volume over €600,000, use of shell entities in tax havens, or broadcaster of forged documentation to customs) raise penalties to 2-6 years. AEAT also applies the 'lista de deudores' public disclosure where threatened debts exceed €1,000,000, and cross-border e-commerce operators are subject to enhanced pandemic-era scrutiny of CoD payment mismatch indicators.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and foreign-investment reporting is also administered by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, including the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and is subject to EU Treaty principles on free movement of capital and payments. The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to applicable sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax rules, prudential controls, and foreign-investment screening. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may generally receive foreign capital, pay foreign suppliers, distribute dividends, repay qualifying shareholder debt, and remit profits without a general exchange-control approval. Dividend and interest payments remain subject to Spanish withholding-tax rules, treaty relief or EU exemptions where applicable, beneficial-ownership requirements, transfer-pricing rules, corporate-law distributable-profit tests, and evidence of tax compliance. Banks may require invoices, contracts, board or shareholder resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, tax-residency certificates, and proof of the commercial purpose before executing higher-risk transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the central bank, convert a prescribed percentage of receipts into euros, or repatriate receipts within a fixed statutory period. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the holder's discretion, subject to bank controls, accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Banks may request transaction evidence and may report statistical information to Banco de España. Cash and bearer negotiable instruments transported into or out of the EU at amounts of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared under applicable EU and Spanish rules. Export documentation, VAT evidence, customs records, payment records, and reconciliation of cash-on-delivery collections should be retained under applicable accounting, tax, and AML recordkeeping periods.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for operating payments, subject to onboarding and transaction limits. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution, including a properly passported provider such as Airwallex's relevant EU-regulated entity, may provide payment accounts, safeguarded balances, foreign-exchange conversion, SEPA payments, and international transfers to a Spanish SL. An EMI account is not a bank deposit and is not equivalent to a Spanish commercial-bank account; balances are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the EU deposit-guarantee scheme. The provider may restrict cash-intensive COD activity, third-party collections, marketplace flows, high-risk corridors, or transactions lacking invoices and end-customer evidence. Cash collection and remittance by logistics providers must be performed through appropriately authorised payment, electronic-money, postal-payment, or cash-handling arrangements and must not be structured as unauthorised money transmission.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch for corporate account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, electronic signatures, and verified corporate records. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, a notarised power of attorney, original or apostilled documents, certified translations, a Spanish-resident signatory, or a physical site visit, particularly where directors, beneficial owners, source of funds, COD cash flows, or emerging-market counterparties create enhanced-risk indicators. The company should maintain a Spanish registered office, documented operating address, identifiable management, and a clear local compliance contact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or beneficial owner with a complex ownership chain, nominee arrangements, trusts, or difficulty identifying the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles and commercial-register extract; complete ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; tax-residency certificates; shareholder register; corporate authorisations; declarations of control; certified translations or apostilles where requested; and independent corporate-registry evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery model involving frequent cash deposits, logistics-company collections, third-party settlement, refunds, or substantial cash turnover inconsistent with reported revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end COD operating memorandum; logistics and payment-service contracts; customer-order records; delivery confirmations; cash-collection and reconciliation procedures; daily settlement reports; cash limits; segregation-of-duties matrix; refund policy; bank-deposit trail; VAT and accounting records; and evidence that all collection and payment intermediaries are appropriately authorised.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from emerging markets, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned territories, opaque intermediaries, or counterparties with adverse-media exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due-diligence files; sanctions and PEP screening logs; beneficial-owner verification; commercial contracts; invoices; customs and shipping records; payment-purpose narrative; country-risk assessment; shipping-route evidence; compliance approvals; and documented escalation and rejection procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, rapid shareholder funding, intercompany transfers, shareholder loans, or funds originating from unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited or management financial statements; tax returns; sale or financing agreements; shareholder resolutions; capital-increase deed where applicable; loan agreement and repayment terms; proof of originating account ownership; source-of-wealth statement; and a funds-flow diagram linking the remitter to the Spanish SL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared ecommerce activity and account activity, including marketplace receipts, payment-processor settlements, personal-account usage, or unexplained high-value transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; website and platform details; supplier and marketplace agreements; expected-volume schedule; product catalogue; geographic customer map; payment-flow diagram; accounting-system extracts; monthly management accounts; tax registrations; and written controls prohibiting personal-account and unapproved third-party use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence beneficial ownership, management control, economic substance, or a credible Spanish operating nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or registered-office evidence; employee or contractor records where applicable; director mandates; board minutes; Spanish tax registrations; supplier and logistics agreements; inventory or fulfilment records; customer-service arrangements; local compliance policy; and documented governance and decision-making procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital through an account held in the name of the Spanish SL, preferably from an account held by the subscribing shareholder or its documented parent, using SEPA credit transfer for euro funding or SWIFT for non-euro funding. The payment narrative should identify the transaction as share capital, share-premium funding, capital increase, or shareholder loan, as applicable; no generic personal-transfer description should be used. Before receipt, prepare the shareholder or board resolution, subscription or loan agreement, notarised capital-increase documentation where applicable, beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds file, and bank account ownership evidence. Reconcile the incoming transfer to the accounting entry and, for a formal capital increase, the public deed and Commercial Registry filing. Review whether foreign-investment statistical reporting, sectoral screening, or other filings apply under Spanish foreign-investment legislation; the receiving bank may request the relevant declaration or filing evidence. Do not route capital through employee, director, logistics, or personal accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and standard bank transfers for other EEA or international payments. Use SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent for cross-border commercial payments, with accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and purpose information. For higher-value or higher-risk purchases, use an irrevocable documentary Commercial Letter of Credit, preferably subject to UCP 600, with specified shipping documents, inspection requirements, sanctions clauses, and discrepancy procedures. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where appropriate. Maintain purchase orders, invoices, contracts, customs declarations, bills of lading or courier evidence, proof of delivery, beneficiary verification, and three-way reconciliation between order, delivery, and payment. COD logistics settlements should be paid only to the contracted authorised collection or payment provider and reconciled to individual orders, returns, refunds, and VAT records. Banks may apply correspondent-bank screening, payment holds, enhanced due diligence, and information requests.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorised bank or investment firm for documented commercial exposures, supported by forecast or confirmed receivables and payables and subject to MiFID II classification, appropriateness or suitability processes, collateral terms, and EMIR requirements where applicable.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or where the banking counterparty offers cash settlement, subject to product eligibility, documented underlying exposure, counterparty credit limits, valuation, collateral, and regulatory reporting requirements.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for matching or refinancing recurring currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, netting enforceability, collateral arrangements, EMIR obligations where applicable, and board-approved counterparty limits.

Plain-vanilla currency options, collars, and option forwards may be used only for genuine commercial hedging and after disclosure of premium, contingent obligations, break costs, valuation risk, and maximum downside; speculative or structurally leveraged products should be prohibited without specialist approval.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions through banks or authorised payment institutions for settlement, working-capital management, and repatriation. Maintain a treasury policy covering permitted currencies, hedge ratios, maturity matching, counterparty limits, valuation, accounting treatment, and prohibited speculative positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (annual statutory accounts deposit with the Mercantile Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; accounts must be deposited within 1 month of approval - effective deadline 30 July for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of €1,200 up to €60,000; closure of the corporate registry record (cierre registral) after 6 months of non-filing blocks all further corporate acts; administrative strike-off (baja registral) after 6 consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 200 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades (annual corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month anniversary of fiscal year-end - 1 to 25 July for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5%-20% of tax due plus late-payment interest at the statutory rate; penalties up to €15,000 for inaccurate or false returns

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Titularidad Real (annual beneficial ownership confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial / Registro Mercantil Central (filed together with the annual accounts deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit - within 1 month of AGM approval (30 July for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and file current UBO data constitutes a serious infringement under AML Law 10/2010, subject to fines from €10,001 up to €60,000; any shareholding change above 25% must be reported within 30 days

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 202 - pago fraccionado (quarterly advance corporate income tax instalments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 20 April, 20 October, and 20 December of each fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at the statutory annual rate (3.75% for 2025) plus extra-fiscal surcharge of 1%-20% depending on the delay period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 390 - Declaración resumen anual del IVA (annual VAT summary return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January following the close of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing recargo of 5%-20% of VAT due plus statutory late-payment interest; material inaccuracies subject to penalties of up to 15% of the affected VAT amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalización de Libros (annual legalisation of the official accounting and corporate books)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end (30 April for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalised books lose evidentiary force in commercial litigation; repeated omission exposes the SL to registry inspection findings and mandatory rectification orders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit applies to an SL that exceeds at least two of three criteria for two consecutive years: (i) total assets over €2,850,000; (ii) net turnover over €5,700,000; (iii) average workforce over 50 employees. Below these thresholds the SL is audit-exempt unless members holding at least 5% of share capital request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad 2007) as amended, aligned with EU-endorsed IFRS; qualifying SMEs apply the abbreviated PGC 'PYME' framework; annual accounts must be filed in XBRL/XML format with the Mercantile Registry.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, together with the annual accounts deposit, the SL must validate and file its register of beneficial owners (libro de titularidad real) with the Mercantile Registry; any transfer of more than 25% of capital or voting rights must be updated in the register within 30 days; the Mercantile Registry verifies UBO continuity at each shareholder change before inscribing the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members / Shareholders)
Libro de Actas (Minutes of members' and board meetings)
Libro Registro de Contratos con Socios y Administradores (Register of contracts with members and directors)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and annual accounts book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - 1,500 per annum for commercial agent, registered office, and annual compliance services in Madrid, Barcelona, or Valencia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for audit-exempt SL below statutory thresholds; USD 4,000 - 8,000 per audit cycle if mandatory audit thresholds are triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official tax return form designation and electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline relative to the fiscal year-end
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Summary of late filing penalties and daily surcharges

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Administrative process to invoke DTA relief and TRC submission
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory and treaty rates for IP royalties and debt interest

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Threshold triggering mandatory Local File / Master File
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
